# Ink Bleed

**Cover › Organic** · v1.0.0 · 90 frames at 30 fps (48–150)

Drops of ink land and spread with fibrous edges until the frame is solid, then the next scene bleeds back through.

[Preview video](https://github.com/GTKottman/remotion-transitions/releases/download/media/ink-bleed@1.0.0.mp4) · [Alpha overlay for editing apps](https://github.com/GTKottman/remotion-transitions/releases/download/media/ink-bleed@1.0.0-overlay.mov)

## Where it is used

- Editorial and artistic edits
- Section breaks
- Calligraphic or handmade brands

## Use it

```tsx
import { linearTiming, TransitionSeries } from '@remotion/transitions';
import { toPresentation } from './src/core';
import inkBleed from './transitions/04-cover/organic/ink-bleed';

<TransitionSeries.Transition
  presentation={toPresentation(inkBleed, { /* params */ })}
  timing={linearTiming({ durationInFrames: 90 })}
/>
```

Use `linearTiming`: the transition applies its own easing. It draws with WebGL, so render with `--gl=angle` (GPU) or `--gl=swangle` (no GPU).

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Default | Range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `color` | color | `"#FF4F1A"` |  | The incoming scene's background colour; the transition brings it in. |
| `drops` | integer | `4` | 1–9 | Number of ink drops. |
| `seed` | integer | `1` | 0–9999 | Changes the random layout. |
| `hold` | number | `0.1` | 0–0.4 | Share of the transition spent fully covered. |
